item.title: A Unified Intermediate Representation and Execution Architecture for Heterogeneous and Distributed Neural Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.23964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Equation-based neural modeling offers flexibility, but executing models across processors and nodes requires explicit control of order, ownership, and numerical behavior. We present brian2-atlas, a rebuilt execution architecture retaining Brian2's modeling interface and bringing heterogeneous and distributed targets under a common model-to-execution contract. Its unified intermediate representation, AtlasIR, describes typed state, clocks, schedules, effects, events, and random-stream identities, and is checked by an independent Rust validator. Target-specific implementations support Rust CPU execution, CUDA and Apple Metal GPUs, browser WebAssembly, and MPI within declared contracts. In a repeated full-connectome CPU cohort, the best measured Rust configuration reduced simulation-and-recording time by 5.43-fold relative to the best measured Brian2 C++ configuration on the same Linux host. A 298.9-million-synapse model completed on a 16 GB laptop while the compared C++ preparation path exceeded its controlled memory budget. Distributed execution completed 100.5 seconds of model time for 4,129,924 neurons and 24.1 billion recurrent synapses on four nodes and 32 ranks. A five-point synthetic weak-scaling study reached 860 million neurons and 860 billion recurrent connections for 100 ms on 30 hosts and 240 physical worker cores. These establish tested capacity configurations rather than statistical equivalence or a matched speed advantage over NEST. Published-model workflows extend validation to explicit NMDA dynamics and contextual dendritic plasticity, with up to 2.10-fold acceleration in a matched eight-core NMDA cohort. The results characterize semantic, numerical, and resource boundaries rather than universal compatibility or performance superiority.
item.dc:creator: Xinjun Li (Next Brain)

item.title: CROPS: Cosserat-Rod-Based Co-Design of Soft Slender Programmable Material Systems for Biomedical Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.24209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Slender structures made of stimuli-responsive materials represent an emerging class of programmable material systems, with applications in soft robotics, minimally invasive surgery, wearable electronics, and deployable structures. In biomedical applications, the on-demand design of slender structures, encompassing both their material layout and actuation, is essential to harnessing their large deformation and multiphysics actuation to meet patient-specific design requirements. However, owing to geometric and material nonlinearities, their structure-actuation-response relationship is highly nonintuitive and computationally demanding. This often makes trial-and-error and conventional design approaches challenging for addressing patient-specific needs. To this end, we present a Cosserat-rod-based design optimization framework for the autonomous design of programmable slender structures. Leveraging the Cosserat rod representation, the end-to-end differentiable framework is demonstrated on two case studies: (i) design of swellable stents that morph to the shape of carotid vessels; (ii) co-design of the remnant magnetization and the applied field of magnetically-active catheters to reduce the force exerted on the patient-specific vessel wall during insertion. Both self-contact and external contact with surrounding structures are accounted for. We consider two actuation mechanism, namely the swelling of gel-elastomer composites and the magnetic actuation of hard-magnetic composites. The proposed framework presents an autonomous design platform of soft slender material systems that support large deformations and multiphysics actuation toward personalized biomedical design.
item.dc:creator: Aaditya Chandrasekhar, Dex Doksoo Lee, Hyunwoo Kwon, Shicheng Li, Wei Chen

item.title: A decomposition-integration framework coupling singular spectrum analysis with a volatility-adaptive LSTM for stock price forecasting
item.description: arXiv:2610.24384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Financial time series exhibit multi-scale, high-noise, and non-stationary volatility dynamics. Decomposition--integration frameworks built on complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) have advanced this field, yet existing CEEMDAN hybrids remain unstable: high-frequency mode mixing contaminates downstream predictors, and the heterogeneous volatility of decomposed components is not matched by any volatility-adaptive mechanism. To address these gaps, this paper proposes CEEMDAN-SE-SSA-VMGL. CEEMDAN adaptively decomposes the original series, and sample-entropy-driven K-means clustering groups the intrinsic mode functions into high-, mid-, and low-frequency and residual components. Singular spectrum analysis (SSA) is then applied to the high-frequency group, whose singular-value decomposition of the trajectory matrix and principal-component reconstruction decouple intertwined pseudo-oscillatory modes and alleviate mode mixing. We further design a plug-and-play robust LSTM variant, the volatility-modulated GARCH-LSTM (VMGL), which embeds a differentiable GARCH(1,1) layer inside the LSTM cell as a risk gate; the estimated conditional volatility multiplicatively scales the forget-gate activation, letting memory decay adapt to the instantaneous volatility while remaining fully end-to-end trainable. Component predictions are linearly combined. On five US and Chinese financial series (CSI 300, CSI 500, AAPL, GOOGL, S&P 500), the proposed model is compared with eleven benchmark architectures, lowering the forecasting error by 9% to 24% relative to the best benchmark and by 60% to 70% relative to a standard LSTM. Diebold--Mariano and model-confidence-set (MCS) tests confirm the statistical significance and stability of the gains, spectral analyses verify the SSA denoising efficacy, and backtesting demonstrates the framework's economic utility.
item.dc:creator: Xin-Rui Lu, Da-Qing Zhang

item.title: Learning volatility-adaptive forgetting via GARCH-modulated LSTM for stock price forecasting
item.description: arXiv:2610.24386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stock price forecasting is hindered by the heteroscedastic nature of financial time series, in which turbulent and tranquil regimes alternate. Although the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network is widely used for this task, its gates are oblivious to such volatility variation, so memory retention remains fixed regardless of market conditions. A common remedy is to supply volatility estimates as an additional input feature, yet this leaves the internal memory dynamics untouched. Instead, volatility can serve as a direct regulatory signal over the gate activation itself. This paper presents the Gsigmoid-LSTM model, which embeds Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroscedasticity (GARCH(1,1))-derived volatility estimates into the LSTM forgetting gate through the Gsigmoid activation function, a volatility-adaptive variant of the sigmoid that combines a volatility adjustment factor with slope regulation via a learnable parameter. The model thereby automatically prioritizes recent information during turbulent periods while preserving long-term dependencies in stable markets. In the engineering application of daily stock price forecasting, extensive experiments, including activation function comparisons, baseline evaluations, and ablation studies, demonstrate that this structural gating modification effectively improves forecasting accuracy and robustness. The proposed model significantly outperforms a feature-level fusion baseline carrying the same volatility signal on all five datasets, as confirmed by Diebold-Mariano tests with all p<0.01, attains the best average rank of 1.00 in the Friedman test across nine models, and achieves the lowest MSE and MAE on all five datasets.
item.dc:creator: Xin-Rui Lu, Da-Qing Zhang

item.title: Do in-silico metrics filter designed enzymes for catalysis?
item.description: arXiv:2610.24437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computational metrics are widely used to prioritize enzyme designs for experimental testing, yet their ability to capture catalytic function remains poorly established. Here, we systematically evaluate 33 in-silico metrics across four complementary tasks: distinguishing active from inactive enzymes, identifying substrate specificity, ranking enzyme variants by activity, and detecting perturbations to catalytic residues. We assess these capabilities using natural enzymes, computationally designed enzymes, activity-altering variants, and controlled structural perturbations that compare catalytic residues with matched non-catalytic sites. No single metric consistently captures all aspects of catalytic function. In activity discrimination, catalytic-residue intra-residue repulsion achieves the highest AUROC among the evaluated metrics for both natural enzymes (0.61) and 192 designs that passed the filters of their original design campaign (0.80). For substrate discrimination, interface predicted TM-score (ipTM) performs best (AUROC 0.70), whereas the catalytic pKa range shows the strongest association with activity across single-point variants of BglB (Spearman's rho = 0.48). In controlled perturbation tests, the minimum per-chain predicted TM-score (pTM) has a mean probability of 0.75 of responding more strongly to perturbations at catalytic residues than to matched perturbations at non-catalytic sites. These results reveal substantial variation in what current computational metrics capture, underscoring the need to distinguish structural confidence and physical plausibility from direct evidence of catalytic function when prioritizing enzyme designs.
item.dc:creator: Ziqi Zhang, Wei Zhang, Zhaohong Deng

item.title: WUI-CAST: Real-Time Forecast Updating for Partially Observed Wildland-Urban Interface Fires
item.description: arXiv:2610.24553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wildland-urban interface (WUI) fires couple landscape spread, structural fire development, and wind-driven ember transport. Forecasting building risk requires models that incorporate emerging observations and update predictions as fires evolve. This study presents WUI-CAST, a framework integrating established fire-propagation representations with sequential Bayesian state estimation to support real-time forecast updating under partial observation. A Dynamic Bayesian Network represents nonlocal ember-driven ignition and local structural propagation, while Bayesian filtering updates building-state probabilities using sparse reports. A retrospective Camp Fire application provides a proof-of-concept evaluation. Open-loop simulations captured key features of the wildfire-to-community transition. In two 30-minute forecasts evaluated against subsequently reported buildings before their assimilation, closed-loop updating increased Recall@10% from 29.03% to 83.87% and from 0.00% to 43.75%, with improved conditional spatial logarithmic scores in both windows. Regional and local diagnostics reveal how assimilation redistributes risk beyond directly observed buildings. Controlled experiments demonstrate gains across the tested observation conditions and filtering implementations. A forecast-update cycle averaged 42 s for a 5-min simulation interval. Together, these findings demonstrate improved spatial risk prioritization from sparse observations and a computationally feasible approach to real-time WUI forecast updating.
item.dc:creator: Can Wang, Naiyu Wang, Yang Zhou

item.title: Permafrost augmented simulation and forecast using hybrid modeling through spectral neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.24665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Purpose - Global warming is impacting several crucial Earth systems, including the permafrost. This study investigates the possibility of performing fast and reliable simulation and forecasting of permafrost behavior, addressing a critical gap in the existing literature related to high computation times and energy costs of the simulations. Methodology - A numerical cryohydrogeological study on water and energy transfer in a forested, continuous permafrost site has been conducted using parallel high-performance computing to simulate the permafrost dynamics. The numerical results reasonably replicate the measured soil temperature profiles and the dynamics of infiltrated waters. This work uses a spectral network to achieve a fast, reliable, and stable surrogate model for the simulations to forecast over long periods of time. The surrogate is also enhanced by assimilating experimental data through the development of a hybrid modeling framework. Findings - The proposed approach improves the physical simulation while maintaining the stability of the dynamic model over long periods of time. The results reveal that the proposed hybrid modeling remains stable in integration and forecasting. The final hybrid solution demonstrates a significant improvement in simulation accuracy when tested against a test set of measurements. Predictions of the permafrost behavior in the coming decade are later made based on the CMIP6 climate change scenarios. Originality - This research offers a novel perspective on permafrost modeling that extends the current understanding of its behavior under different climate change scenarios. It shows a higher-than-expected temperature increase of the permafrost. Moreover, the stable forecasting of climate change effects is demonstrated.
item.dc:creator: Chady Ghnatios, Thibault Xavier, Anatoly S. Prokushkin, Laurent Orgogozo, Francisco Chinesta

item.title: Enabling the 1 1 Promise AI Enabled Fairness for Indonesia Retail IPO Allocation
item.description: arXiv:2610.24706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Indonesia OJK Circular, effective November 2025, requires that half of every IPO pooled allocation go to retail investors. Uniquely amongst major capital markets, the regulation places all non-institutional participants, regardless of wealth, into a single competing pool rather than separating them by monetary thresholds. The rule is structurally sound; however, enforcement and measurement of effectiveness require methods beyond rule-based detection alone. Well-resourced participants operating within the retail pool can distribute bids across networks of synthetic retail accounts, each individually compliant, allowing them to capture the retail quota without triggering standard concentration heuristics. Without a mechanism to detect such networks before allotment closes, the statutory guarantee of equal access becomes procedurally hollow: the quota is formally reserved for retail households while the economic benefit flows elsewhere. We present a framework for identifying such nominee networks using eleven statutory fields already collected by Indonesia e-IPO infrastructure, requiring no new surveillance powers or personal data. The paper shows that when a Global South regulator prioritizes genuine inclusion over administrative convenience, algorithmic enforcement becomes both feasible and necessary.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of the AAAI ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society date 11 Oct 2026
item.dc:creator: Anchal Gupta, Gleb Papyshev, James T Kwok

item.title: On the near-field evolution of a chemically reactive plume behind a ship
item.description: arXiv:2610.24947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The near-field evolution of chemically reactive pollutants in the exhaust plume of a 270 m crude oil tanker is investigated using a high-fidelity Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) framework coupled with a Conditional Moment Closure (CMC) turbulence-chemistry interaction model and the CBM-IV atmospheric chemistry scheme. Two complementary approaches, a canonical zero-dimensional CMC (0D-CMC) and a spatially resolved Imperfectly Stirred Reactor Network (ISRN), quantify micromixing effects using information from the CFD flow field. Micromixing strongly modulates the evolution of NO, NO2, O3, and PAN, explaining spatial discrepancies between detailed CFD-CMC results and Gaussian plume estimates. While conventional Gaussian formulations overpredict near-field NO by up to 45% within the first 300 m, they are used here as a contextual reference to highlight where turbulence-chemistry coupling matters. The CFD-CMC-ISRN framework therefore provides a physically consistent basis for integrating micromixing effects into next-generation dispersion and air-quality models. This framework bridges the gap between combustion-derived turbulence-chemistry models and environmental dispersion simulations, enabling improved parameterization of subgrid mixing in regulatory contexts.
item.dc:creator: Ramesh Kolluru, Savvas Gkantonas, B Harikrishnan, Epaminondas Mastorakos

item.title: A $u$-$p_w$ SPH framework with mechanical-hydraulic boundary treatment in GeoDualSPHysics for large-deformation geomechanics
item.description: arXiv:2610.25175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pore-water pressure changes the effective stress and deformation of saturated geomaterials, while skeleton deformation generates pressure and drives drainage. Resolving this feedback together with hydraulic boundary conditions is necessary for simulations that connect consolidation to large post-failure movement. This paper presents a hydromechanical extension of GeoDualSPHysics using a single-layer displacement-pore-water-pressure ($u$-$p_w$) smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) framework. An explicit pressure-rate equation combines volumetric compression and Darcy diffusion, and the resulting pore pressure feeds back into the skeleton momentum balance. The implementation extends the existing modified dynamic boundary condition (mDBC) infrastructure to carry hydraulic ghost values alongside mechanical boundary data. Prescribed pressure at drained surfaces is combined with impermeable walls and impermeable loaded contacts, with separate control of loading and drainage activation. The formulation is assessed through one-dimensional consolidation, two-dimensional flexible-strip loading, and the three-dimensional Cryer problem. The Cryer simulations reproduce the non-monotonic central pressure response over four Poisson ratios, with normalized pressure root-mean-square errors of 0.012-0.030. The consolidation tests also expose remaining settlement and late-time pressure discrepancies. Applications to 5 m and 8 m sensitive-clay slopes illustrate sequential retrogressive failure and large deformation. The contribution is the integration of hydraulic feedback and boundary handling within GeoDualSPHysics; the results establish an initial verification basis while identifying remaining accuracy and convergence questions.
item.dc:creator: Yangfan Ma, Bin Su, Zheng Han, Changze Li, Mitsuteru Asai

item.title: HP-GSBS: Accelerating greedy state boundary search with reusable interval statistics
item.description: arXiv:2610.25898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Greedy State Boundary Search (GSBS) identifies transitions between relatively stable neural activity patterns, but repeated candidate evaluation makes large analyses expensive. HP-GSBS is an open-source Python package that reorganizes the search around reusable interval contributions and correlation statistics. Streaming candidate reduction and local refinement further reduce repeated work; CPU, PyTorch CUDA and Triton backends share sequential segmentation decisions. Across seven controlled workloads with two realizations each, median same-input speedups range from 154 to 1730 times. All 168 optimized executions reproduce original boundaries and selected state counts, with maximum absolute t-distance difference $1.88\times10^{-11}$. Four frozen EEG recordings provide complementary validation, including a complete input-to-segmentation application example. Batch processing, versioned result persistence and optional low-memory execution support recording collections and longer inputs. By removing redundant computation, HP-GSBS makes established neural-state segmentation faster while preserving its scientific outputs.
item.dc:creator: Yanzhe Zhao, Yongzhang Ji

item.title: Surface matching for image-derived geometries with a projection-based separation of rigid body modes
item.description: arXiv:2610.26238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The large diffeomorphic deformation metric mapping (LDDMM) framework offers numerous techniques for analyzing shapes and images. Surface matching computes a non-rigid, smooth, and invertible mapping that registers one surface to another. The computed deformation may contain rigid body motion, which frequently does not represent meaningful shape differences but is due to external factors like imaging modalities, such as the object's positioning during image acquisition. We present a simple extension to the LDDMM framework's surface matching that uniquely decomposes the computed deformation into rigid body modes (RBM) and RBM-free motion by introducing a suitable projection. This enables a focused analysis of each component individually and additionally helps to preserve the surface discretization quality. Three sets of examples illustrate our approach. A small-scale example demonstrates the proposed method's effects, followed by an example using a single pair of heart geometries, and finally an example involving a cohort of 98 heart shapes.
item.dc:creator: Ludwig Wagm\"uller, Christian Bilas, Markus Gitterle, Michael Wibmer, Michael W. Gee

item.title: Composable, Knowledge-Driven Disservice Propagation for Complex Interdependent Services with a Flow-Allocation Module Validated Against Hydraulic Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modeling cascading failure across interdependent critical infrastructure requires either a composable physical simulator per domain or a topological abstraction that discards quantity awareness. Simulators are costly, data-hungry, and require detailed calibration per domain; topological abstractions stay data-parsimonious while missing quantity-based behaviors that govern real dynamics. We present, instead, a knowledge-driven propagation architecture in which heterogeneous service dependencies are identified by categories: a general logical propagation resolves multi-dependency and redundancy structures purely from how nodes are categorized, while quantity-aware categories plug in dedicated mechanisms - here, a max-min fair-share flow module for water distribution. Both share one discrete functionality scale and a monotonic update algorithm guaranteeing convergence in finitely many rounds. We assess the flow module by comparing its results with those we get from preexisting pressure-driven simulation with WNTR (Water Network Tool for Resilience) on eight realistic networks across four failure families (clustered damage, capacity-targeted attack, source failure, tank loss). Under capacity-targeted attack and source failure a topological-reachability baseline misses 46% of the truly critical junctions, where the flow module misses 10% and 8% at an average critical-class precision of 0.73. Supplementary materials, code and results are available at: https://github.com/cascade-platform-org/CASCADE
item.dc:creator: Cristian Curaba, Stefano Grimaz

item.title: Clue-Guided Money Laundering Group Discovery
item.description: arXiv:2606.26189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Money Laundering Group Discovery (MLGD) aims to identify hidden criminal groups and recover their complete structures in large-scale financial networks. Existing graph anomaly detection methods mainly produce node-level risk alerts, while global group discovery methods passively search for suspicious groups over the whole network. Both are mismatched with real Anti-money-laundering (AML) investigations, where analysts usually start from a concrete clue and gradually expand the investigation to recover the responsible group. To address this gap, we propose Clue-Guided Group Discovery (CGGD), where a laundering group is progressively recovered from an initial clue set through analyst interaction. We further propose Clue2Group, a framework that first constructs a compact local investigation context to reduce noise and preserve chain-like and cycle-like laundering structures. It then estimates a clue-conditioned local risk field with a multi-semantic local-temporal GNN, and finally integrates risk, structural, and prior-pattern evidence to recover a coherent laundering group. Experiments on two large-scale AML benchmarks show that Clue2Group provides a practical clue-driven analysis framework for AML investigations, offering a feasible step toward bridging the gap between graph-based AML research and real investigation workflows.
item.dc:creator: Boyang Wang, Jianing Cao

item.title: Sequence-to-Sequence Neural Surrogate Modeling of Transient Responses in High-Speed Links with Variable Design Parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.24141v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) neural surrogates for high-speed transient response modeling and signal integrity analysis in fixed and variable design parameter spaces. To identify the structural requirements for prediction accuracy, multiple neural architectures were evaluated with respect to different training strategies such as sample-based and unit interval-based, as well as input configurations such as TX-only and TX+RX. For fixed design parameters, feedforward neural networks achieve accuracy comparable to recurrent models while requiring lower computational cost, as the static mapping can be approximated by fully connected and non-sequential representations. Variable design parameters alter the electromagnetic characteristics of the interconnect, which creates parameter-dependent temporal dynamics that require sequence-aware architectures to resolve the evolving interactions within the transient response. The results based on a 14-dimensional variable design parameter scenario show that while autoregressive TX+RX feedback suffers from severe phase drift and error propagation under variable conditions, non-autoregressive TX-only inference leads to stability. To overcome the structural limitations of standard decoders, a recurrent Early Fusion LSTM is proposed, which injects design parameters at the initial encoding stage. This approach achieves superior prediction accuracy, with an RMSE of 31.0 mV and an R2 of 99.51% for transient waveform prediction, an RMSE of 30.7 mV and an R2 of 99.57% for eye-height prediction, and an RMSE of 19.5 ps and an R2 of 99.94% for eye-width prediction. These results demonstrate that neural seq2seq surrogates are accurate for transient response modeling and signal integrity analysis in complex variable design parameter spaces.
item.dc:creator: Julian With\"oft, Shayan Ghanbari, Werner John, Emre Ecik, Ralf Br\"uning, J\"urgen G\"otze

item.title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.25389v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Empirical studies of electricity prices routinely state that their models use only information available at the time of the trading decision. For weather-driven forecasts drawn from commercial archives, this condition is harder to meet than it appears, and whether it holds can change over time. We identify three timing pitfalls. A forecast run is labelled by the issue time of its weather model, but becomes available hours later and keeps changing after publication. Auction gates follow local clock time, while archives use UTC. Outturn series are revised after publication without earlier values being kept. Using the timestamps of 128,656 forecast runs from ten weather-model configurations, matched to the day-ahead and first intraday auction gates in Great Britain over 2022-2026, we find that selecting "the latest run issued before the gate" picks a run not yet published at the gate on more than 99% of delivery days for six of the ten configurations at one of the two gates. For GFS at the day-ahead gate, the share is 0.6% in winter and 99.8% in summer. The exposure also shifts as publication delays drift, and an action margin of a few minutes can cost a full six-hour forecast cycle. The wrongly selected inputs differ materially from those available at the gate, but their apparent accuracy gain ranges from -9% to +24% across variables, models, gates and seasons, so its effect cannot be assumed and must be measured. We argue that point-in-time correctness is a dynamic property of the data pipeline, and propose a protocol that audits it from timestamps before any model is fitted.
item.dc:creator: Abdelkrim Alfalah

item.title: Hybrid metaheuristics for architectural design optimization under small evaluation and wall-clock budgets
item.description: arXiv:2610.26202v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Architectural and structural design optimization in parametric software affords about a thousand evaluations of an expensive model for problems with tens of variables, a regime for which most metaheuristics were not designed. On the side of artificial intelligence, two hybrid metaheuristics are proposed: a covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) whose sampling is enriched with differential-evolution trial vectors, and a particle swarm with success-history parameter adaptation, differential-evolution injection and local refinement. A budget-aware delay of population-size reduction in adaptive differential evolution is also proposed. Under a hard cap of 1,200 evaluations, all counted, the CMA-ES hybrid ranks first on seven shifted and rotated functions at 10 and 30 variables and beats CMA-ES on six of seven functions at 30 variables. Ablations attribute this gain to the injection and show that a local search pays off only when its result re-enters the population. The delayed schedule improves three adaptive differential-evolution variants in 40 of 51 comparisons, with no loss. On the side of engineering application, in Grasshopper the CMA-ES hybrid and plain CMA-ES are never significantly worse than the optimizers of Galapagos, SilverEye, Opossum and Tunny on travelling-salesman instances and on a built 85-variable free-form shell, where they end 48 % below the best external tool in 15 minutes. On a 22-variable building-performance problem with binary choices, differential evolution leads instead. Shifting and rotating the functions reverses the rank of Harris hawks optimization. Solvers should therefore be selected by problem structure and stopping time, not by a single ranking.
item.dc:creator: Luciano Ambrosini

item.title: Toward Structured Financial Foundation Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.26516v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Foundation models promise reusable capabilities and step-change performance gains across tasks. In finance, large-scale pretraining of domain-specialized foundation models can advance both goals. However, prevailing architectures and objectives do not by themselves address the combined demands of financial systems: partial observability, interacting entities, asynchronous events, changing regimes, action-dependent outcomes, and rare states with disproportionate consequences. Moreover, independently developed specialists may learn incompatible representations, while multi-domain monolithic alternatives couple data access, model updates, and governance. We therefore propose a structured-data-first research agenda centered on modular, domain-specialized financial foundation models connected by a representation fabric for reuse and composition across domains and tasks. These models should maintain persistent financial state across aggregation levels and time horizons, capture its dynamics, and simulate action-conditioned futures, while remaining calibrated across regimes and for tail outcomes. They must also learn efficiently under data and access constraints and provide faithful, traceable explanations. We identify research challenges, directions, and capability-oriented evaluation criteria.
item.dc:creator: Natraj Raman, Saumitra Mishra, Vamsi Potluru, Sumitra Ganesh

item.title: EBCC v0.2: Error bounded compression for weather and climate applications
item.description: arXiv:2510.22265v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As the resolution of weather and climate simulations increases, the amount of data produced is growing rapidly from hundreds of terabytes to tens of petabytes. These data volumes limit broader adoption, and their continued growth will soon exhaust available storage capacity. To address this problem, we present EBCC v0.2 (Error Bounded Climate-data Compressor). EBCC follows a two-layer compression approach: a base layer using JPEG2000 to capture the bulk of the data at high compression ratios, and a residual layer storing sparse wavelet coefficients to eliminate long-tail extreme errors efficiently. It supports three-dimensional chunks through a multicomponent transform (MCT) in the base layer. To achieve error bounded compression, we introduce error-bound-aware rate allocation in the JPEG2000 base layer. It selects coding passes to approximately satisfy the error target while optimizing the trade-off between compression ratio and mean squared error. We evaluate EBCC alongside established compression methods on benchmarks relevant to weather and climate science, including error statistics, sequential and parallel throughput tests, case studies of primitive and derived variables near a tropical cyclone, an analysis of global energy-budget closure, and a Lagrangian air-parcel trajectory simulation. EBCC either outperforms or closely follows the strongest existing baseline across these benchmarks at relative error targets ranging from 0.01% to 10%, achieving compression ratios from 15x to more than 300x. In the energy-budget-closure and Lagrangian-trajectory benchmarks, EBCC achieves more than 100x compression while keeping compression-induced errors below an assimilation-uncertainty reference derived from the ERA5 uncertainty ensemble. These results demonstrate that EBCC can produce heavily compressed weather and climate datasets suitable for downstream applications.
item.dc:creator: Langwen Huang, Luigi Fusco, Florian Scheidl, Jan Zibell, Michael Armand Sprenger, Alexandru Calotoiu, Sebastian Schemm, Torsten Hoefler

item.title: Mode-Weighted Transport Certificates for State-Dependent Reflected Switching Diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2608.01992v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: State-dependent switching diffusions can contract in law even when individual modes are expansive. We establish a computable, constant-one contraction certificate on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and compact convex domains with normal reflection. The mode-weighted transport cost combines spatial separation with a discrete graph penalty and retains spatial dependence when the modes differ. A synchronous Brownian coupling and a maximal coupling of jump clocks in equal modes lead to separate equal- and unequal-mode generator inequalities. We give a complete regularization argument for the nonsmooth cost, including the drift and jump errors, the sign of reflection, and the limiting It\^o-Dynkin calculation. A resolvent proof transfers contraction to probability-valued weak solutions of the no-flux Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov system, while an explicit Foster-Lyapunov condition ensures existence and uniqueness of an invariant law on the whole space. For fixed weight ordering and decay rate, certificate synthesis is a semi-infinite linear feasibility problem; on compact domains, a Lipschitz-buffered finite mesh provides a rigorous test. One-dimensional and planar examples illustrate the certificate and its numerical verification.
item.dc:creator: Yutong Zhu, Ye Zhang

item.title: VeriFin: A Neurosymbolic Framework for Verifying LLM-Generated Financial Claims
item.description: arXiv:2608.10213v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models often produce plausible numerical claims from financial filings while using the wrong reporting period, unit, line item, or formula. Verifying such claims requires more than rechecking arithmetic: a verifier must ground the relevant facts, establish the authorized calculation, and determine whether the candidate value follows from both. We propose VeriFin, a neurosymbolic verification framework for numerical financial question answering that grounds operands in filed XBRL facts, derives calculations from the question, filing linkbases, or documented metric definitions, and checks claims using Z3. When a claim is inconsistent, solver-derived unsatisfiable cores identify the conflicting facts, formula, and candidate value, enabling targeted repair. We evaluate VeriFin on XBRLFiling, a new 600-question benchmark constructed from 10-K filings of 28 U.S. companies, and on FinanceBench. On fixed candidate pools shared by all verification methods, VeriFin accepts none of the incorrect claims, whereas the baselines accept 6 to 92 incorrect claims on XBRLFiling's 600 claims and 4 to 21 incorrect claims on FinanceBench's 67 claims. The zero false-accept result persists across multiple answer-generator models. Solver-derived feedback further improves repair, achieving up to 69.9% recovery among true catches. These results show that source-grounded symbolic verification can provide a reliable and auditable acceptance control for LLM-generated financial claims.
item.dc:creator: Bethel Hall, Sachi Shome, William Eiers

item.title: How the Classical Baseline Shapes Machine-Learning Speed Claims in Topology Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.16051v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Topology optimization places material in a design domain to optimize a structure's performance, such as its stiffness or heat conduction. Machine-learning methods often report large speed-ups over classical, non-learned optimization, but a slow classical code or a lower-quality learned design can exaggerate them. We re-ran released code for eight methods on one workstation and studied two in depth: Optimize Any Topology (OAT), a diffusion model that generates designs, and a graph-based neural optimizer. Replacing the classical code with an efficient implementation of the same algorithm cut these two methods' speed-ups by up to 20-fold. We then timed the classical code until its design was at least as stiff as the learned one; for OAT, we picked this point after the runs, which gives the classical code its best case. Published timings imply a 134x speed-up for OAT on a 256 x 256 grid; our matched single-design comparisons gave 1.5x to 3.5x. At matched stiffness, the graph-based optimizer was slower than the classical code in all six two-dimensional problems. Of the six other methods, two kept their advantage, one shrank, one reversed, and two were not comparable. In an exploratory audit, language models judged that 8 of 28 speed comparisons in randomly sampled, openly accessible articles lacked evidence of equal design quality; our own review counted 11, so the count depends on who judges. We provide a comparison procedure and a minimum report: classical code, hardware, design quality, what each timing includes, and data-generation and training costs.

item.title: BizAgentBench: Unveiling Hidden Challenges in Deploying Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Business
item.description: arXiv:2610.20424v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing long-horizon agent benchmarks often emphasize final task success while providing limited assessment of intermediate execution validity. Yet real-world business operations require agents to navigate extensive, potentially outdated or conflicting policies while satisfying critical constraints throughout execution. These requirements are particularly consequential in high-stakes domains such as payments, where intermediate violations can incur financial losses or regulatory consequences regardless of the final outcome. To bridge this evaluation gap, we introduce BizAgentBench, a multi-turn benchmark grounded in real-world procedures from a leading payments company. Its executable environment integrates 789 knowledge documents and 601 discoverable business tools, with consistent policies, states, and tool behavior. The benchmark comprises 50 tasks involving resource constraints, temporal dependencies, prior commitments, and conflicting or outdated guidance. Each task is validated through reference execution, while deterministic checks assess both goal attainment and execution validity without prescribing a single solution path. Experiments reveal substantial limitations even among frontier models: Claude Opus 5 and GPT-6 Sol achieve strict success rates of only 64.0% and 61.3%, respectively. For Qwen3.8-27B, goal attainment reaches 42.0%, but strict success drops to 32.7%, demonstrating how outcome-based evaluation can mask invalid execution. Beyond success rates, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash averages 191.3 tool calls per run, approximately 70% more than reference executions, revealing substantial execution overhead. Overall, BizAgentBench establishes a testbed for evaluating and advancing long-horizon agents beyond task completion, toward reliable and constraint-compliant execution in complex business environments.

item.title: Buffer-Parameterized Machine Learning Surrogate Models for Cross-Technology Signal Integrity Analysis and Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2605.18170v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Signal integrity (SI) analysis in printed circuit board (PCB) interconnects faces increasing complexity due to diverse integrated circuit (IC) buffer technologies, varying operating conditions, and manufacturing tolerances. Existing machine learning (ML) surrogate models for the prediction of SI metrics such as the inner eye contour, eye-height (EH), eye-width (EW), and transient waveform features often rely on fixed buffer parameters, limiting the adaptability across design and technology variations. This paper introduces a buffer-parameterized ML surrogate modeling methodology capable of handling cross-technology variations without retraining by treating IC buffer characteristics, e.g., clock frequency, supply voltage, rise/fall times, jitter, and internal resistors and capacitors, as model inputs in addition to the PCB parameters. To identify the optimal surrogate architecture for this high-dimensional space, tree-based methods (RFR/GBM), kernel methods (SVR/KRR), Gaussian process regression (GPR), and neural networks are compared. The buffer-parameterized approach is validated using a complex interconnect with a total of 44 design parameters. In addition to demonstrating strong generalization, the results show that neural networks outperform other ML models on large datasets, while the anisotropic GPR excels in low-data regimes. Finally, the practical value of the ML surrogate models is demonstrated through a cross-technology design space exploration and optimization scenario, which indicates large computational speedups for eye mask compliance checking compared to simulation.
